blocks.html: Imagine a school without a principal. Teachers would not know which class to take, rooms would be double-booked and nobody would keep the records. The operating system (OS) is the principal of the computer: it manages every resource and makes sure each program gets what it needs.
Definition: An operating system is system software that manages the computer's hardware and software resources and provides an interface between the user and the computer.

blocks.html: Booting: when you switch on the computer, the BIOS/UEFI in ROM checks the hardware (POST — Power-On Self Test) and then loads the operating system from the disk into RAM. This is called booting. Starting from power off is a cold boot; restarting a running computer is a warm boot.

items.html: Microsoft Windows — the most used OS on desktops and laptops.
macOS — on Apple computers.

Linux — free and open-source; anyone can study and change its code. Versions (distributions) include Ubuntu and Fedora. India's C-DAC developed BOSS Linux (Bharat Operating System Solutions) with support for Indian languages.
Android — by Google; based on Linux; runs most smartphones in India.
iOS — on Apple iPhones.

blocks.html: After Windows starts and you sign in, you see the desktop — your work area.

rows: Small pictures that stand for programs, files or folders; double-click to open
Has a small arrow; opens a program or file stored elsewhere
Holds deleted files until it is emptied; files can be restored from here
The bar at the bottom showing open and pinned programs
Opens a list of all apps, settings and the power options
Finds apps, files and settings by name
Clock, volume, network, battery and notifications

items.html: Title bar — shows the name of the program or file.
Minimise, Maximise/Restore and Close buttons — at the top-right.
Menu bar or Ribbon — commands grouped under tabs.
Scroll bars — move the view up/down or left/right.
Status bar — information at the bottom, such as the page number.

blocks.html: A dialog box is a small window that asks for information, e.g. the Save As box. It has buttons such as OK, Cancel and Apply.

items.html: A file is a named collection of data stored on a disk — a letter, a photo, a song or a program.
A folder (directory) is a container that holds files and other folders (sub-folders).

blocks.html: A file name has two parts: name.extension, for example Science_Project.docx . The extension tells Windows what kind of file it is and which program opens it.
A file name in Windows cannot contain these characters: \ / : * ? " < > |
The path is the full address of a file: drive, then each folder, separated by backslashes.
C:\Users\Riya\Documents\Class9\Science_Project.docx

blocks.text: Working with files in File Explorer

blocks.html: Open File Explorer with Windows key + E.

rows: Right-click an empty space → New → Folder, or Ctrl + Shift + N
Select the item and press F2, type the new name, press Enter
Select → Ctrl + C → go to the new place → Ctrl + V (original stays)
Select → Ctrl + X (cut) → go to the new place → Ctrl + V (original is removed)
Shift + Delete (does not go to Recycle Bin)
Open Recycle Bin → right-click the file → Restore
Ctrl + click for separate items, Shift + click for a range, Ctrl + A for all

blocks.html: Open Settings with Windows key + I. From here you can change:

items.html: System — display brightness, resolution, sound, battery saver, storage.
Personalisation — background, colours, lock screen, themes.
Accounts — user accounts, password, PIN, fingerprint.
Time and language — date, time zone, add Hindi keyboard (InScript or phonetic).
Apps — install or uninstall programs.
Windows Update — security updates and fixes. Keep it on.

blocks.html: The older Control Panel still offers many of these settings.

rows: Simple plain-text editor; good for writing C++ code too
Shows running programs; ends a program that is not responding (Ctrl + Shift + Esc)
Ctrl + C / Ctrl + X / Ctrl + V

blocks.html: Click Start → Power:

items.html: Shut down — closes all programs and switches off.
Restart — shuts down and starts again (needed after some updates).
Sleep — uses very little power and resumes quickly.
Sign out — closes your session so another user can sign in.

blocks.html: Never switch off the computer from the main power switch while it is running; unsaved work may be lost and files may be damaged.

items.html: The operating system manages processes, memory, files, devices and security, and gives the user an interface.
Booting loads the OS into RAM; cold boot starts from power off, warm boot is a restart.
Types: single-user, multitasking, multi-user, real-time, batch and mobile OS. CLI uses typed commands; GUI uses icons.
Windows desktop: icons, taskbar, Start menu, search, notification area, Recycle Bin.
Files have names and extensions; folders hold files; a path gives the full address.
File Explorer is used to create, copy, move, rename, delete and restore files.
